lines.japanese: 「各駅停車・柳木原行き、ドア閉まりまーす」
lines.english: “Local service for Yanagihara. The doors are closing.”

lines.japanese: 「お荷物、お体、お引きください」
lines.english: “Please stand clear with your belongings.”

lines.japanese: 地上を走る地下鉄に積みこまれて、僕は大都市・柳木原へ運ばれる。
lines.english: Packed aboard a subway train running aboveground, I was carried toward the metropolis of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 新聞を広げるスペースさえない満員の車内は、利きすぎた暖房と、おびただしい人いきれとで、胃がもたれそうだ。
lines.english: There was not even room to open a newspaper in the crowded car. The overzealous heat and the breath of countless bodies were enough to turn the stomach.

lines.japanese: 冷たいドアと無数のスーツに容赦なく押しつぶされながら、僕は白い空を見ていたくてぎりぎりの空間で首を伸ばす。
lines.english: Crushed without mercy between the cold door and a multitude of suits, I stretched my neck through the last inch of space, wanting to keep the white sky in sight.

lines.japanese: 知らないおじさんのポマードがこびりついた分厚いガラス窓の向こうに、柳木原の高層建築が見えてきた。
lines.english: Beyond the thick glass, greased with some stranger’s pomade, the high-rises of Yanagihara came into view.
“Whoa…!”

lines.japanese: 運転士が未熟な制動をかけた拍子に、乗車率２００％オーバーの車内が大きく揺れた。どどっと音を立てて、安定を失った何十何百という身体が折りかさなったまま進行方向へ傾く。
lines.english: The driver applied the brakes with an amateur’s touch, and the car—loaded beyond two hundred percent capacity—lurched violently. With a single heavy rush, tens and hundreds of bodies lost their balance and tipped together in the direction of travel.

lines.japanese: 乗客はみな周囲の名も知らぬ他人にだけは貸しを作るまいと、必死で壁や柱や吊革にすがった。
lines.english: Every passenger clung desperately to wall, pole, or strap, determined not to do any favors for the nameless strangers around them.

lines.japanese: 僕も白い空の覗くガラス窓、流れゆく高層ビル群に張り手を叩きこんで不安定な身体を支えた。しかしそこに別なる危機──
lines.english: I caught my unsteady body by slapping a palm against the window, against its glimpse of white sky and procession of passing towers. Then came another danger—

lines.japanese: 「痛っ！」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: ──足の甲に、痛みを伴う重みが落ちてきた。
lines.english: —a painful weight descended upon the top of my foot.
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: 失態、といったニュアンスの息遣いが、僕の顎の下から聞こえた。
lines.english: A breath tinged with mortification came from somewhere beneath my chin.

lines.japanese: 「す、すみませんっ！」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry!”

lines.japanese: 気が付けば美空学園指定の見慣れた女子用コートの肩が、前のめりの負荷と戦いながら僕の胸板にのしかかっている。差し色のパステルブルーは二年生の学年色。そしてローファーの踵は、体重ごと僕の左足へ。
lines.english: The shoulder of a familiar girls’ coat in Misora Academy colors was bearing against my chest, struggling under the forward crush. Its pastel-blue accent marked her as a second-year. The heel of her loafer, meanwhile, rested on my left foot beneath the whole of her weight.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ、や……え、ええっ……！？」
lines.english: “Oh—what? I… What do I…?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は深く下向いたまま、見知らぬ上級生男子の靴を踏んづけているという状況から一刻も早く逃れるべく、僕の胸の中でもがく。至近距離の体からふわりと果実の香りがした。
lines.english: Head bowed low, she struggled against my chest, desperate to escape the fact that she was standing on the shoe of an upperclassman she had never met. A soft scent of fruit rose from her body at such close quarters.

lines.japanese: しかし乱暴に減速してゆく満員電車の床には、激しく揺すぶられたばかりの足という足が、すでに隙間なくがっちり打ちすえられている。新たに足を置きかえる余剰空間が見つからないようだった。
lines.english: But the floor of the packed train, still decelerating with brutal force, was already paved solid with feet that had just been violently shaken from their places. There seemed to be no spare inch in which she could set hers down anew.

lines.japanese: 「あああ、ごめ、ごめんなさい……足が、あの、足がどかせなくて……！」
lines.english: “I’m so, so sorry… My foot—I can’t, um, I can’t move it…!”

lines.japanese: 俯いて表情を伏せているけれど、真っ赤になった耳の裏までは隠せていなかった。
lines.english: She kept her face hidden, but could not conceal the crimson backs of her ears.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの……あのうっ、すみ、すみません、ちょっ、と……」
lines.english: “Um… Excuse me, I’m sorry, could you just…”

lines.japanese: 頼みごとをするのが苦手そうな震える声と、遠慮がちに押しだそうとする前腕で、彼女は真横の中年女性に懇願している。しかし暖簾に腕押し、ぎちぎちに固まって動けないのは前後左右の誰もが同じだった。
lines.english: With a trembling voice plainly unused to asking favors and a forearm pressing timidly outward, she pleaded with the middle-aged woman beside her. But it was no use. Everyone around us was packed just as tightly and just as incapable of moving.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ」
lines.english: “It’s all right.”

lines.japanese: 僕は、封を開けた板チョコが割れてたときみたいな失笑を漏らした。
lines.english: A rueful laugh escaped me, the sort you give when you unwrap a chocolate bar and find it already broken.

lines.japanese: 「大して痛くないし」
lines.english: “It hardly hurts.”

lines.japanese: どうせ不運慣れしている僕には、この程度のことなんて災難のうちにも入らない。
lines.english: I was accustomed to bad luck. Something this small did not even qualify as misfortune.

lines.japanese: それに、なぜだか今朝は気分がいいんだ。いまの僕なら、ジャマイカの漁村あたりで日がな一日パイプをくゆらせる老人のように、ほほ笑みひとつで何だって許せる。
lines.english: Besides, for some reason I was in a good mood this morning. Just now, I felt I could forgive anything with a smile, like an old man spending all day smoking his pipe in a Jamaican fishing village.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あああ、すみません先輩……ほんとに、ほんとに申しわけありません……」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry... I'm truly, truly sorry...”

lines.japanese: 彼女は足元へ目を落としたまま、泣きの入った声でひたすら謝りつづける。
lines.english: Her eyes remained fixed on our feet as she apologized without end, on the verge of tears.

lines.japanese: 「いいってば」
lines.english: “I said it’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 僕はふたたび首を伸ばして彼方の白い空を眺めた。顔も見えない下級生に踏まれつづける痛みが、やがて効きの悪い局所麻酔のように感覚を鈍らせてゆく。
lines.english: I craned my neck once more toward the distant white sky. The pain of being continually trodden on by a faceless underclassman gradually dulled my senses like a weak local anesthetic.

lines.japanese: 僕は知っている。痛みを忘れること、痛みを痛みと認識しないこと、それがこの白い空の下で健やかに生きるための妙諦だ──机上の論理だけど。
lines.english: I knew the secret: forget pain; refuse to recognize pain as pain. That was the profound truth of living in health beneath this white sky—if only in theory.

lines.japanese: 緩やかに平衡を取りもどしてゆく満員電車の中、押しつけられる制服越しの体温を意識しながら、僕は改めて思った。女の子の肩って卑怯なくらいに細いんだな。
lines.english: As the crowded train slowly regained its balance, I became conscious of the warmth pressed against me through our uniforms and thought anew: a girl’s shoulders were unfairly slight.

lines.japanese: 「やなぎはらー、やなぎはらー」
lines.english: “Yanagihara, Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「終点ー、柳木原です。お忘れ物ないようご注意ください」
lines.english: “This is the final stop, Yanagihara. Please take care not to leave any belongings behind.”

lines.japanese: すし詰めの車両に押しこまれていた乗客たちが、蒸した空間から逃げるように、先を争ってホームへ飛びだしてゆく。
lines.english: The passengers who had been stuffed into the car burst onto the platform in a race to escape the steaming enclosure.

lines.japanese: 最後まで顔を上げなかった恥ずかしがり屋の下級生も、俯いたままの会釈をしつつ、流れる降車の波に乗ってそそくさと去っていった。
lines.english: The shy underclassman, who had never once raised her face, bowed without looking up and hurried away on the tide of disembarking bodies.

lines.japanese: 開いた扉の反対側にいた僕はそれらの背中をゆっくり見送り、あとからひとり悠々と降りた。
lines.english: I had stood opposite the doors that opened. I watched their backs recede, then stepped leisurely off the train alone.

lines.japanese: 暖房の効きすぎた密室から改札口めざして行進する僕らを、ひゅるりと渡った追い風が後押しする。
lines.english: As we marched toward the ticket gates from that overheated chamber, a tailwind whistled through and urged us onward.

lines.japanese: 五分もすれば呪うことになる冬の寒さも、いまはまだ汗ばんだ体が歓んで迎えいれている。
lines.english: The winter cold I would curse in five minutes was, for now, welcomed gladly by my perspiring body.

lines.japanese: 北風とエアコン。世界の厳しさと優しさが入れかわる、そんなひとときがたまにあるよね。
lines.english: The north wind and air-conditioning. Sometimes the world’s cruelty and kindness trade places for a moment.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 自動改札を抜け、駅構内のフラワーショップを通りすぎたあたりで、鮮やかな黄色が目に飛びこんできた。
lines.english: After I passed through the automatic gates and went by the flower shop inside the station, a brilliant yellow leapt into my eyes.

lines.japanese: 菊の花束を肩に担いだ、僕と同じ制服の背中が前を歩いている。
lines.english: Ahead of me walked someone in my school uniform, a bouquet of chrysanthemums resting on one shoulder.

lines.japanese: 体の線は女のひとみたいに細くてしなやかだけど、褐色の肌や幅広の肩や無造作に散らされた黒髪や、なにより空気を切りさくような歩き方が彼の気性をよく表している。
lines.english: His figure was as slender and supple as a woman’s. But his brown skin, broad shoulders, carelessly scattered black hair, and more than anything the way he walked as though cleaving the air before him spoke plainly of his temperament.

lines.japanese: 同じクラスの針生さんだ。僕にとって──あるいはクラスの誰にとっても──３年Ａ組男子の中で、もっとも近寄りがたい存在。
lines.english: It was Hariu from my class: to me—and perhaps to everyone—the least approachable boy in Class 3-A.

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間、わけもなく僕の視線は脇へ走り、体は彼と逆の方へ向いていた。
lines.english: The next instant, for no reason I could name, my eyes darted aside and my body turned away from him.

lines.japanese: 校外で思いがけずクラスメイトに出くわしたとき、思わず身を隠したくなるのは僕だけじゃないはず。
lines.english: Surely I was not the only person who wanted to hide when he unexpectedly encountered a classmate outside school.

lines.japanese: だけど、ふと思いだしてしまった。
lines.english: Then I remembered.

lines.japanese: “６：クラスに友達をつくる”
lines.english: “6. Make a friend in class.”

lines.japanese: だから僕は、後ろから小走りで近づいていった。
lines.english: And so I trotted up behind him.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん」
lines.english: “Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 僕より身長の低い、だけど僕よりずっと大人びた雰囲気を放つ体が、億劫そうに振りかえる。途中、通学鞄を持った方の手の甲が、すばやく左の脇腹へ添えられた。
lines.english: The figure before me, shorter than mine but possessed of a far more adult presence, turned with evident reluctance. Midway around, the back of the hand holding his schoolbag darted to his left side.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: レンズの奥で、僕を捕えた鋭い目が一瞬膨らみ……またすぐに細くひずんだ。
lines.english: Behind his lenses, the sharp eyes that had caught me widened for an instant, then narrowed once more into a scowl.

lines.japanese: 音もなく僕を凝視する彼の名は、針生蔵人。
lines.english: The boy staring soundlessly at me was Kurodo Hariu.

lines.japanese: 同じクラスだけど、年齢は僕よりひとつ上──つまり、彼は三年生を二度繰りかえしている。理由は知らない。良くない噂ならいくつか風に乗ってきているけれど。
lines.english: We were classmates, but he was a year older than me—which meant he was repeating his third year. I did not know why, though several ugly rumors had drifted my way.

lines.japanese: 「あの……おはよう、ございます……」
lines.english: “Um… Good morning…”

lines.japanese: 返事がない。威圧的な眼光が揺るがないように、その唇もまた固く閉ざされたままだ。浅い溜息のような呼吸音だけが緩やかに鼻から抜けてゆく。
lines.english: No answer. His lips remained as tightly sealed as his intimidating gaze remained steady. Only the sound of his breath, like a shallow sigh, passed slowly through his nose.

lines.japanese: 僕は教室で小耳に挟んだ、インテリヤクザという彼の仇名を思いだす。針生さんは全国レベルでもトップクラスの学力を誇っているけれど、出席状況や生活態度の面では常に教職員一同を悩ませていた。
lines.english: I remembered the nickname I’d overheard for him in class: the Honor-Roll Gangster. Hariu was one of the country’s brightest students, but his attendance and conduct were a constant headache for the entire faculty.

lines.japanese: 居心地の悪い視線に耐えかねて、僕は踏みだしたことを後悔した。ホームから冷たい北風が渡って、余熱を失いかけた体に吹きつける。
lines.english: Unable to endure his disquieting stare, I regretted ever approaching him. A cold north wind crossed the platform and struck my body, now losing the last of the train’s heat.

lines.japanese: 冬がもう牙を剥いた。テスト前に風邪をひくわけにもいかないから、僕は急いで立ちさることにした。そう、それだ。
lines.english: Winter had shown its fangs already. I could hardly afford to catch cold before an exam, so I decided to hurry away. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、お先に──」
lines.english: “Well, I’ll go on ahead—”

lines.japanese: 「おい」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: しかし、いざ通りすぎようとしたら、冷たい声で呼びとめられた。鋭い命令が乾いた空気に染みる。
lines.english: But as I moved to pass him, his cold voice stopped me. The sharp command cut through the dry air.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes?”

lines.japanese: 僕は足を止めて相手を窺った。針生さんは花束ごと右手の中指を鼻筋へ持ってゆき、そっと眼鏡のブリッジを押しあげた。
lines.english: I stopped and watched him. Still gripping the bouquet, Hariu raised the middle finger of his right hand to the bridge of his nose and gently pushed up his glasses.

lines.japanese: 「誰だおまえ」
lines.english: “Who are you?”

lines.japanese: お魚くわえた野良猫にでも誰何するような、しらけきった一声。
lines.english: He sounded utterly bored, as though questioning a stray cat caught with a fish in its mouth.
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 同じクラスになって八ヵ月も経つのに、僕はまだ顔すら覚えられていなかった。僕の存在ってなんだろう。コンコースに風が吹きぬける。
lines.english: Eight months in the same class, and he had yet to remember my face. What was I, then? Wind swept through the concourse.

lines.japanese: いや、仕方ない。彼は学校を休みがちだし、どう見ても積極的にクラスの輪に溶けこむタイプじゃない。そう、それだ。
lines.english: No, it could not be helped. He was often absent, and by no stretch of the imagination was he the sort to enter eagerly into the life of the class. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「３Ａの羽田鷹志です」
lines.english: “I’m Takashi Haneda from Class 3-A.”

lines.japanese: 僕はある程度の笑顔をこしらえて名乗った。
lines.english: I introduced myself behind a reasonably convincing smile.

lines.japanese: 「はねだ？」
lines.english: “Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの眉間に稲妻みたいな皺が走ったかと思うや、訝しげな視線が僕の制服を上から下までひと舐めしていった。
lines.english: A lightning-bolt crease flashed between Hariu’s brows. His suspicious gaze licked slowly down my uniform from head to foot.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、うちの学校──」
lines.english: “You go to my school—”

lines.japanese: そして戻ってきた目でふたたび僕の表情を捕えたとき、彼の口元が初めてほころんだ。
lines.english: When his eyes returned and caught my face again, his mouth softened for the first time.

lines.japanese: 「──しかも３Ａ。はン、俺と同じクラスだったのか」
lines.english: “—and you’re in 3-A. Hnh. So we’re in the same class.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、３Ａの学級委員です」
lines.english: “Yes. I’m the class representative for 3-A.”

lines.japanese: 僕個人のパーソナリティを知らなくても通じるだろう説明に変えてみた。
lines.english: I tried an explanation that might mean something even if he knew nothing of me personally.

lines.japanese: 「学級委員」
lines.english: “Class representative.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは肩を揺らしながら復唱した。吹き出すときに少し俯きがちの伏目になる仕草は、トーク番組に駆りだされたはにかみ屋のミュージシャンみたいだ。
lines.english: Hariu repeated it, his shoulders shaking. When laughter made him lower his face and eyes, he looked like some shy musician dragged onto a talk show.

lines.japanese: 「なら教壇に立ったりしてるはずだなァ。フー、まいった、印象になかったよ」
lines.english: “So you get up in front of the class and stuff, then. Whew, you got me. Guess you didn’t leave much of an impression.”

lines.japanese: 目を伏せたまま、肩を揺らす。そういえば、彼が指されたいつかの授業で、話をするときは相手の目を見ろと注意されていたのを思いだした。
lines.english: Eyes still lowered, he shook with laughter. I remembered a lesson when the teacher had called on him and then admonished him to look at people when he spoke.

lines.japanese: 「学校行かないもんなあ俺。行ったところでまあ、この顔は覚えてねえだろうけど」
lines.english: “Then again, I never go to school. Even when I do, I doubt I’d remember a face like yours.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの投げやりな言葉はあさっての方向へこぼされているので、ああこれは僕に言ってるのじゃなくて単なる独り言なんだろうな、と割りきることにした──
lines.english: Hariu let the indifferent words spill out into empty air, so I decided they must be mere soliloquy rather than anything addressed to me—

lines.japanese: ──のだけど、ふと彼が思いだしたようにおもてを上げた。
lines.english: —but then he suddenly looked up, as though remembering something.

lines.japanese: 「ああ！　ってことは、明日香のツレだおまえ」
lines.english: “Ah! So you’re Asuka’s guy.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「今カレはクラス委員だって聞いたけどなァ……違うの」
lines.english: “I heard her current boyfriend was the class rep… Have I got the wrong man?”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、いや……はい……」
lines.english: “I… Um… No…”

lines.japanese: いきなり渡来さんの下の名前が呼び捨てにされてる。針生さんは彼女と親しい仲なんだろうか。たしかに、ふたりが話している場面なら何度か見かけたことはあった。
lines.english: Without warning, he was calling Watarai by her first name. Were the two of them close? Now that I thought of it, I had seen them talking several times.

lines.japanese: 「ふッ」
lines.english: “Hnh.”

lines.japanese: 何がおかしいのか、彼はまぶたを伏せて鼻を鳴らした。
lines.english: Whatever amused him, he lowered his eyelids and snorted.

lines.japanese: 「あァ～、ああ！　なるほど、そうか、こいつがそうなのか……はン、そりゃあ明日香が目を付けるわけだ。相変わらずそういう臭いに気付く嗅覚は大したもんだなァ、あいつ」
lines.english: “Ahh… Ah! I see. So this is him… Hnh. No wonder Asuka noticed you. Her nose for that particular stink is as keen as ever.”

lines.japanese: 「あのう、渡来さんが何か……」
lines.english: “Um… Is there something about Watarai…?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あァ、何かはあるけどまあ、口止めされてるから答えられないなあ」
lines.english: “Hm? Ah, there is something, but I’ve been sworn to silence, so I can’t tell you.”

lines.japanese: 今日は寒い一日になりそうだなあ、とでも呟くような調子で、針生さんはしれっと言った。
lines.english: Hariu said it blandly, in the tone one might use to observe that it looked like being a cold day.
“Ha… ha…”

lines.japanese: それが年長者流の冗談なのか何なのかさっぱり分からなかったけど、僕には相槌としての曖昧な愛想笑いで流すことしか出来なかった。
lines.english: I had no idea whether this was some older boy’s idea of a joke or something else altogether. All I could do was offer a vague, obliging laugh and let it pass.

lines.japanese: 「ふうン……そうか、そういうこと」
lines.english: “Hmm… I see. So that’s what’s going on.”

lines.japanese: 「ハハ、なるほどね、やりようによっちゃ面白いことになりそうだ。けど、ンー……下手は打てないしなァ、どうしたもんか……」
lines.english: “Ha ha. I see. Depending on how I play this, things could get interesting. But, hmm… I can’t afford to make the wrong move. What now…”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは眼鏡の裏に厳しいしわを寄せ、口元だけで笑う。頭は僕の方を向いているけど、瞳はすでに僕を捕えていない。目に映る景色とは違うところに焦点を絞っているみたいだ。
lines.english: Severe creases formed behind Hariu’s glasses, while his mouth smiled alone. His head faced me, but his eyes had already released me. They seemed focused on something other than the scene before them.

lines.japanese: 「いっそおまえの腹をかっさばいて、呑まれた宝珠を引きずりだしたいね」
lines.english: “I’m half inclined to slice your belly open and drag out the jewel you swallowed.”

lines.japanese: 彼は線路工事の案内掲示でも眺めながら、実に軽々しくそんなことを言った。ごほ、と喉のつかえを払いながら左の脇腹に触れる。
lines.english: He said this with astonishing lightness while gazing at what appeared to be a notice about track repairs. He touched his left side and cleared an obstruction from his throat with a cough.

lines.japanese: 「冗談だよ」
lines.english: “A joke.”

lines.japanese: 正面に向きなおって真顔で付けくわえられたけど、僕にはどこが笑いどころなのか理解できなかったし、そもそも僕に対して放たれた言葉だとも思わなかった。
lines.english: He turned back to me and added this with a perfectly grave face. I could not identify where the humor lay, nor had I even thought the preceding words were meant for me.

lines.japanese: 「鳳凰寺カケルって知ってる？　ヘッタクソなくせに、黒板を爪で引っかくような嫌らしい感性を絵にする野郎だよ。あいつの作品──落書きに、そんなテーマのものがあったなァと、いま不意に思いだした」
lines.english: “Do you know Kakeru Hououji? He’s a talentless hack who puts that nasty fingernails-on-a-blackboard feeling into his art. I just remembered one of his works—his scribbles—had a theme like that.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はあ……そうなんですか……」
lines.english: “Oh… I see…”

lines.japanese: そういえば針生さんはしばしば図書室で、教員しか近寄らないような棚を物色している。また、一時期は校外の仲間とバンドを組んで、それなりにライブハウスを賑わせていたなんて噂も聞く。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Hariu often prowled the library shelves that only teachers approached. I had also heard rumors that for a time he played in a band with friends outside school and drew respectable crowds at music clubs.

lines.japanese: 趣味はゲームや漫画ばかり、人付き合いと言えばほとんどオンラインＲＰＧとソーシャルネットワークで完結している僕とでは、きっと思考も感性も周囲の環境も違いすぎるんだろう。
lines.english: My interests began and ended with games and manga; nearly all my dealings with other people took place inside online RPGs and social networks. Our thoughts, our sensibilities, our entire surroundings must have been worlds apart.

lines.japanese: なんだか急に会話の空隙が気になりだして、ふたたび後悔の波が押しよせてきた。
lines.english: Suddenly, the gaps in our conversation became impossible to ignore, and another wave of regret washed over me.

lines.japanese: 声をかけるにしてもまだ早かった。同じ制服を着ている以上、目的地は同じなんだ。ここから校門そして教室まで、僕は彼と並んで歩く時間をどうやり過ごせばいいんだろう。
lines.english: I had spoken to him too soon. We wore the same uniform, so our destination could only be the same. How was I to survive walking beside him from here to the school gates, and then all the way to our classroom?

lines.japanese: 「まァ、でも、同じクラスのやつに会えてちょうど良かった」
lines.english: “Still, good thing I ran into someone from my class.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんが唐突にそんなことを言うから、僕は一瞬驚いてしまった。
lines.english: The abrupt remark took me by surprise.

lines.japanese: 「委員長、おまえ、教室にこれ持ってってくれる」
lines.english: “Class Rep. Take this to the classroom for me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、あ、はい……」
lines.english: “Oh. Um, all right…”

lines.japanese: 彼は通学鞄から５００ミリペットのミネラルウォーターだけ抜きとり、残りを僕の胸に押しつけてきた。手を出さなければ落ちてしまう。受けとらざるを得なかった。
lines.english: He pulled nothing but a half-liter bottle of mineral water from his schoolbag and thrust the rest against my chest. If I did not put out my hands, it would fall. I had no choice but to take it.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　学校行かないんですか？」
lines.english: “Wait. Aren’t you going to school?”

lines.japanese: 「先にちょっと寄るとこあンだ。身内に不幸があったのを今日知ってなァ」
lines.english: “I’ve got somewhere to stop first. Found out today there was a death in the family.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは冷静な声で言うと、そう大きくはない菊の花束を肩に載せた。
lines.english: Hariu said it calmly and settled the modest bouquet of chrysanthemums on his shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　いまからですか？」
lines.english: “What? You’re going now?”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだって言ったでしょう」
lines.english: “…I believe that is what I just said.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、すいません、でも、もうまっすぐ学校行かないと、遅刻しちゃいますよ」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. But if you don’t go straight to school now, you’ll be late.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは時計見りゃ分かるよ、ファッキンボーイ」
lines.english: “I can read a clock, fuckin’ boy.”

lines.japanese: 年上のクラスメイトは低く速く答えた。冷たい北風が通る。彼は顔をしかめながら二つ三つ大きな咳払いを挟んだ。
lines.english: My older classmate answered low and fast. A cold north wind passed through. Grimacing, he broke off for two or three heavy coughs.

lines.japanese: 「真面目だな。でも俺は委員長じゃない、問題ないだろ」
lines.english: “How earnest of you. But I’m not the class rep, so there’s no problem.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 僕に対する皮肉を、彼は通りすぎる駅員を観察しながら言った。ひとところに視点が定まらないのは癖みたいだ。しかし冷ややかな三白眼は、落ちつきない子供よりも油断ない狩人をイメージさせる。
lines.english: He delivered the barb while observing a station attendant passing by. His gaze seemed habitually unable to rest in one place. Yet those cold, white-rimmed eyes suggested a vigilant hunter rather than a restless child.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、そうじゃなくて……あの、だって今日は期末テストですよ？」
lines.english: “No, that isn’t what I mean… Today is the final exam.”

lines.japanese: 「二度も言わせるなよ。俺はおまえじゃないんだ、追試でも再試でもいくらだって埋め合わせが──」
lines.english: “Don’t make me say it twice. I’m not you. Makeups, retakes—I can recover the loss any number of ways—”

lines.japanese: 「──んんンっ、かっ、こふっ」
lines.english: “—nnngh, kh—koff!”

lines.japanese: どうにも喉が絡むらしい。針生さんはミネラルウォーターのキャップをねじ切って口を付けた。ラベルに描かれた冠雪の連山が逆さまになって、透明の液体に泡が立ちのぼった。
lines.english: Something was badly caught in his throat. Hariu twisted the cap from his mineral water and drank. The snowcapped range on the label turned upside down, and bubbles climbed through the clear liquid.

lines.japanese: 「……そういうことだ」
lines.english: “…That is the point.”

lines.japanese: 足元に息を落とし、彼はミネラルウォーターに詮をした。空いた手が、左の脇腹に移る。何度か見せるその仕草が、僕はちょっと気になっていた。
lines.english: He let a breath fall toward his feet and capped the bottle. His free hand moved to his left side. I had noticed him make the gesture several times, and it troubled me a little.

lines.japanese: 「あの……ひょっとしてそこ、怪我してるんですか？」
lines.english: “Um… Are you hurt there, by any chance?”

lines.japanese: へその横あたりを押さえている彼の手を見下ろした。五本の指が制服の生地に皺を作っていた。
lines.english: I looked down at the hand pressed beside his navel. Five fingers creased the fabric of his uniform.

lines.japanese: 返事がないので目を上げると、そこで視線がぶつかった。彼は笑っていた。
lines.english: When no answer came, I looked up and our eyes met. He was smiling.

lines.japanese: 「羽田？　つったっけ？　ふッ、気安いなあ委員長」
lines.english: “Haneda, was it? Hnh. You’re awfully familiar, Class Rep.”

lines.japanese: ひどく冷たい笑い。忙しなくさまよっていた針生さんの黒目が、ぴたりと僕に狙いを定めていた。
lines.english: It was a terribly cold smile. Hariu’s black eyes, which had wandered ceaselessly until then, fixed their aim upon me.

lines.japanese: 「なあ、おまえにも、他人に言えない話のひとつやふたつはあるよなァ？」
lines.english: “You have a secret or two you can’t tell anyone, don’t you?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「なら分かれよ。誰にだって、言いたくても言えないことはあるんだ、むやみに干渉するなって」
lines.english: “Then understand. Everyone has things they can’t say, however badly they might wish to. Don’t go prying.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ！　おれはべつに、そんなつもりじゃ……」
lines.english: “No! I didn’t mean anything like that…”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、悪いけどこれだけは言わせてもらいましょう。明日香に選ばれたって点だけでも、おまえには好奇心をそそられるよ。でも感情的なことを言えば委員長、俺はおまえみたいないじけた子供が嫌いなんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, forgive me, but I will say this much. The fact that Asuka chose you is enough to stir my curiosity. But speaking from the heart, Class Rep, I detest self-pitying children like you.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 刺された。凍えた風がプラットホームから自動改札を抜けて、僕の中を貫通していった。
lines.english: The blade went in. A freezing wind came off the platform, passed through the ticket gates, and pierced straight through me.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな。鞄たのんだよ」
lines.english: “See you. Take care of the bag.”

lines.japanese: 駅東口──つまり学校とは正反対の繁華街方面へ歩きだす年上の同級生を、僕は最後まで見送らなかった。
lines.english: I did not watch my older classmate all the way as he set off toward the station’s east exit—toward the shopping district, in precisely the opposite direction from school.

lines.japanese: 北風がどこかから砂埃を運んできたようで、口の中がざらついて咳が出た。ここは空気が淀んでいる。
lines.english: The north wind must have carried dust from somewhere. Grit roughened my mouth and made me cough. The air here was stagnant.

lines.japanese: 「こ、こふっ……ごふ、ごふっ……」
lines.english: “K-koff… Koff, koff…”

lines.japanese: 咳きこんで頭が揺れると、景色も一緒に揺れた。僕は喉元を押さえてひゅうひゅう喘ぎながら、残る片手に自分と他人の鞄を握って雑踏を掻きわけた。
lines.english: The coughing shook my head, and the world shook with it. Clutching my throat and wheezing, I gripped both my own bag and another’s in my remaining hand and forced a path through the crowd.

lines.japanese: 早く出口へ。早く外へ。１２月の白い空が恋しくて、なんだか息が詰まりそうだった。
lines.english: The exit. I had to reach the outside. I longed for December’s white sky, and suddenly I could scarcely breathe.

lines.japanese: そんなとき僕のポケットにあったのはいつだってペロリチョコ。コイン一枚おいしさ二倍、あの日の夕陽がよみがえる懐かしの甘さ。いちご味も新発売。
lines.english: At times like this, there was always Perori Chocolate in my pocket. One coin, twice the deliciousness—the nostalgic sweetness that brings back that sunset. Now in strawberry, too.

lines.japanese: 僕は小さな駄菓子の包みを解いて口の中に放りこんだ。
lines.english: I unwrapped the little piece of penny candy and tossed it into my mouth.
